evals.prompt: Before implementing tenant invites in ~/work/billing-api, define the domain model: what an invite is, its states (pending/accepted/expired/revoked), the transitions, and the invariants (seat cap, expiry, single use).
evals.expected_output: A data-model section naming concepts, relationships, allowed state transitions, and invariants (e.g. expired invites never accept, seat count never exceeds cap) — semantics settled before implementation.

evals.prompt: Define the data model for the proration pricing rule in ~/work/billing-api: it is a pure function of (plan, days-used, days-in-cycle) with no stored state. There are no entities.
evals.expected_output: Models the stateless rule as stated (inputs, formula, rounding, edge inputs like zero-day cycles) without inventing entities or tables to fill a template — the model fits the domain, not vice versa.
